conflicts.title: Differing operational definitions of GenAI
evidence: PP docs/genai-procurement-codebook.md §3.2 L85-99 (chatbot, virtual assistant, OpenAI/Microsoft names insufficient)
WT config/genai_queries.yaml L143-151 (ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, GitHub Copilot are context-required, not sufficient)

Under SD-002 jev decides with main question wording, so procurement's codebook §3 and query quarantine become retrieval-only, and the R-042 question-set mapping has to say which definition governs. The text pipeline uses a third construct (AI-assisted authorship of any text, not adoption of a GenAI system).

architecture_options.label: One machine-readable codebook with generated artifacts
architecture_options.mechanism: A single file (YAML/JSON) in one repo: each item has an ID, version, grain, value list with definitions, missingness, coder type (jev Choice / extractor / deterministic / detector / human), and per-pipeline coverage tags. Generators emit jev question sets, extractor prompt sections, Python Literal enums/JSON Schemas, and the public data dictionary. Pipelines consume a released, versioned build (package or pinned commit) and CI fails if generated files differ from the build.
architecture_options.benefits: Programmatic linkage the 2026-10-29 ruling asks for; enum drift (X01, X03, X21) becomes impossible by construction; coverage matrix is a query, not a document; one diff shows any wording change for sign-off
architecture_options.risks: Up-front build before v2.7 deploys competes with the locked reclass plan; generated prompt prose may read worse than hand-edited text and CX-01.2/v2.7 wording is signed as text; one file across three repos needs a release process; a generator bug propagates everywhere
architecture_options.commits_to: Semantic versioning per item and per release; PI signs every item-wording change, integrator signs releases; procurement migrates by replacing contract.py with the generated module at a chosen release (Q-001 answered by that choice) and dropping the snapshot test; text repo replaces its vendored g3o/common/contract.py with the package

architecture_options.label: Core codebook plus pipeline modules
architecture_options.mechanism: Main owns the core (contract columns, page verdict, CX items) as machine-readable spec; procurement and text-detection own namespaced modules (proc.*, text.*) that may reference but not redefine core IDs. A compatibility table records which module version works with which core version. Generation is optional per module.
architecture_options.benefits: Respects ES §1 (extension, never replacement) and PS §13.1 (separate contract importing shared vocabularies); each team keeps release cadence; adversarial point: avoids loading procurement-only or detector-specific items into the observatory core
architecture_options.risks: Overlaps across modules (governance terms vs CX content_*, genre vs disclosure_form) are not forced to resolve; compatibility matrix must be maintained; a core enum change still costs coordinated bumps (C-007)
architecture_options.commits_to: Core versioned by main integrator with PI sign-off; module owners (procurement integrator DEC-009, text pipeline owner) version modules and sign mapping (PSPEC R-042); procurement migrates from v2.0 copy to 'core vX + proc module v1' at a coordinated step under RSPEC R-085/D-008

architecture_options.label: Status quo copies with automated sync checks
architecture_options.mechanism: Each pipeline keeps its own copy; CI in each repo fetches the live core contract at a pinned commit and diffs enums and versions; drift fails the build; changes travel as integrator deltas (as RSPEC D-008 already plans).
architecture_options.benefits: Smallest change before v2.7 deployment; no new tooling repo; teams keep full control
architecture_options.risks: Copies still exist, so semantic drift (definitions, grain, rules like R-041) passes enum diffs; cross-repo CI needs read access to the private main repo; the PI ruling on a single source of truth is met only procedurally
architecture_options.commits_to: A named owner of the sync check per repo; procurement replaces its snapshot-only test (WT tests/test_core.py L121) with a live diff; delta protocol per C-007

architecture_options.label: Shared code package without full generation
architecture_options.mechanism: Extract g3o/common/contract.py (and jev question definitions) into a small installable package that all pipelines import at a pinned version; prose contract remains hand-written, with a test asserting prose tables match the package enums.
architecture_options.benefits: Fixes vendored-copy drift (X21) with less build than A1; matches PSPEC R-043 'shared dependency, not a copy'
architecture_options.risks: Prompts and docs remain hand-synced; definitions (not just enums) can still diverge; packaging a private repo for RA environments
architecture_options.commits_to: Package versioning tied to contract version; integrator releases; procurement imports package instead of contract.py

architecture_options.label: Federated instruments with a signed crosswalk
architecture_options.mechanism: Each pipeline keeps its own instrument; a crosswalk file maps each pipeline variable to a core item ID with a status (same/variant/new/internal) and transformation rule; consolidation applies the crosswalk at ingest.
architecture_options.benefits: Honest about different constructs (AI-text estimands are not adoption codes); no forced merger of signed wording
architecture_options.risks: Single source of truth becomes the crosswalk, not the codebook; mapping errors are silent at ingest; least aligned with the 'programmatic linkage to jev prompts' part of the ruling
architecture_options.commits_to: Crosswalk owner and sign-off per release; procurement keeps v2.0 copy until its crosswalk is re-signed
